Vañó family olive groves date to 1780; brand-as-marketed launched 2003 by Rosa and Francisco Vañó. NOTE: Olive Oil Lovers reports 2014 as 'formally founded'; this is a >2yr conflict resolved per Decision 6 by using the primary source (2003). Pre-2003 production was bulk oil, not consumer-branded premium.
Founded by Rob McGavin and Paul Riordan in Australia. First grove planted 1998; commercial launch to market 2001 (≤2yr rule: use earlier year).

Estate has been in Colonna family since early 1800s; 'dal 1986' tagline on official site marks the brand-as-marketed founding. Marina Colonna inherited estate from father in 1996. APPROXIMATE — primary source uses tagline rather than explicit founding year.

Five-generation family business; 'over 80 years' per oliveoilsitaly.com places founding ~1940s. APPROXIMATE — no source provides exact founding year for Savino Muraglia senior's mill. Estimated from generational arithmetic and 80yr+ reference.

Frescobaldi.com reports brand-as-marketed year 1988; consortium first bottling 1989 (Manicaretti, Olive Oil Professor, Biordi). 1-year conflict ≤2yr rule: use earlier year (1988). Consortium formed 1986 after 1985 frost; first commercial bottling 1988-1989.
Founded by Andrew Benin; viral squeeze-bottle DTC olive oil brand.
Founded by Katerina (Katina) Mountanos. Name is portmanteau of founder's name and husband's name (Kostas).
Founded by Bruno Bozzini in Italy; now part of Cobram Estate portfolio. Brand year preserved per acquisition rule.
Founded by Armando Manni in Tuscany; trademark MANNI® Oil with 'Live Oil' methodology developed with University of Florence and CNR.

Nan Tucker McEvoy planted first olive trees on Marin County ranch in 1990. APPROXIMATE — primary source year confirmation pending; founded year inferred from McEvoy's biography and ranch establishment timeline.

Family olive oil production traces to 1795 (Baena, Andalucía). Modern premium organic brand launched 1986 by the three Núñez de Prado brothers (Paco, Andrés, Felipe); first organic certification in Spain 1990. Brand-as-marketed pivot follows Castillo de Canena precedent (modern brand year, not estate tradition). Pre-1986 production was bulk oil, not premium branded.

Olio Verde brand released 1989 by Gianfranco Becchina; estate purchased and restored 1985. Brand-as-marketed = 1989 (first commercial release of the brand-named oil). First Sicilian monocultivar olive oil.
Founded by Adi Dassler in Herzogenaurach, Germany after split from brother Rudolf (who founded Puma 1948). Brand 'Adidas' registered 18 August 1949.
Founded by Golden Harper in Utah. Known for zero-drop heel and FootShape toe box design. Acquired by VF Corporation 2018 (brand year preserved per acquisition rule).

Predecessor Onitsuka Co. Ltd. founded 1949 by Kihachiro Onitsuka; 1977 merger with GTO and JELENK formed Asics Corporation. Brand-as-marketed 'Asics' starts 1977 — 'Onitsuka Tiger' was the separate prior brand (and remains a retro line within Asics). Per Decision 6 ('brand-as-marketed'), use 1977 rename year — analogous to Castillo de Canena precedent (modern brand year, not parent corporate heritage).

Founded by Morris Goldenberg in Philadelphia, PA as Brooks Shoe Manufacturing Co. Multiple bankruptcies and re-organizations across 20th century; brand identity continuous. Owned by Berkshire Hathaway since 2006.

Founded by Nicolas Mermoud and Jean-Luc Diard in Annecy, France as 'Hoka One One'; acquired by Deckers Outdoor 2013 (brand year preserved per acquisition rule); rebranded to 'Hoka' in 2021 (brand year preserved per reformulation rule).
Founded by William J. Riley in Belmont, Massachusetts as 'New Balance Arch Support Company'. Family-owned (Davis family) since 1972.

Predecessor 'Blue Ribbon Sports' founded by Phil Knight and Bill Bowerman 25 January 1964 in Eugene, Oregon. Renamed to Nike Inc. 30 May 1971; swoosh logo and Cortez running shoe introduced same year. Brand-as-marketed 'Nike' starts 1971 — analogous to Asics 1977 and Castillo de Canena 2003 (modern brand year wins, not predecessor corporate heritage).

Founded by Nick and Willa Martire in Montreal, Canada in early 2020. First commercial sale July 2021 (≤2yr rule: use earlier year, 2020). Some sources list 2021 as founding year — these reference the commercial-launch year, not the company-founding year.
Founded by Olivier Bernhard, David Allemann, and Caspar Coppetti in Zurich, Switzerland. CloudTec sole technology launched same year.
Founded by Rudolf Dassler in Herzogenaurach, Germany after split from brother Adi (who founded Adidas 1949). Brand 'Puma Schuhfabrik Rudolf Dassler' registered 1 October 1948.
Founded by François Salomon, Jeanne Salomon, and Georges Salomon in Annecy, France. Originally a ski/winter sports brand; running shoes line added 1990s. Owned by Amer Sports.
Founded as Saucony Manufacturing Company in Kutztown, Pennsylvania, USA. Acquired by Wolverine World Wide 2005 (brand year preserved per acquisition rule).
Founded by Tony Post (former Vibram FiveFingers president) in Massachusetts. Known for low-drop, wide toe-box trail and road running shoes.
